text.content:
Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} — Introduction ("From the Treaty of Tyre"), signed 1496.

The Treaty of Tyre is the binding pact between the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} (the Elders and childer of Clans @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian}) and Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} that ended the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}'s first and only clan-wide Blood Hunt (declared in 1486). Its core provisions, as recorded, are as follows:

  • The Clan Assamite shall refrain from taking the Blood of other Kindred, and as surety of this provision shall submit to a ritual administered by the Elders of Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} whereby Kindred blood is made poisonous to them (the origin of the Tremere Curse afflicting the clan — see "The Tremere Curse (Pre-Breaking Weakness)" in this same compendium).
  • The Clan Assamite shall remain peacefully within the territory ceded to them by the Camarilla (their historical claim in the Middle East), seek no expansion of it, and not permit unrest among their mortals to spread beyond it. They shall not travel outside this territory, singly or in groups, nor send Retainers or Servitors beyond it on their behalf.
  • The Princes of the Camarilla retain the perpetual right to call a Blood Hunt against any Assamite within their fiefs, and need give no reason beyond membership in the Assamite bloodline.
  • The defenses of the castle of Alamut shall be dismantled to the point that it can no longer withstand a Camarilla siege or attack. The Camarilla may send observers to verify compliance. Any re-fortification of Alamut, or establishment of a fortification elsewhere, is a breach subject to a worldwide Blood Hunt.
  • The Camarilla undertakes to cease all action against Clan Assamite and not violate the borders of their territory without sanction of a full Camarilla Convocation.
  • The Clans of the Camarilla agree among themselves to no longer employ Assamites as hired assassins; violators forfeit their clan's protection and may be subject to a Blood Hunt. Clan Assamite undertakes to cease all activity of its members as assassins for hire.

Storyteller/LARP note: Many Assamites view the Treaty as a token capitulation to Camarilla paranoia, honored only so far as convenient. Despite the treaty's letter, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} records reputedly list over 2,000 names of Assamites hired for assassination contracts since 1496 — whether through impostors, alternate identities, or quiet Camarilla hypocrisy is left ambiguous by the clan's own chroniclers. The Treaty and its curse remained in force until the Assamites' modern-nights "Breaking" (1998), at which point ur-Shulgi shattered the curse; Storytellers running games set before 1998 should apply the pre-Breaking weakness in full (see companion page).

pages.name: Clan Structure: Alamut, the Castes, and the Du'at

text.content:
Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite}, Chapter Two ("Prayers to Broken Stone").

The Assamites (Children of Haqim) maintain a hierarchy unrivaled among clans besides the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}, seated at their mountain fortress of Alamut. This structure has frayed under the modern-nights Schism (the split between the loyalist ur-Shulgi, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}-allied al-Ashrad, and the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}'s @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} antitribu), but its offices remain reference points for the clan on any side of that divide.

The Three Castes: The clan is divided into three hereditary castes, functionally separate bloodlines (a warrior always sires warrior childer, a vizier always begets viziers, and so on), though all three share the instinctive gift of Quietus and are otherwise indistinguishable in vitae:

  • Warriors (once "judges") — the clan's defenders, assassins, and soldiers; the caste most known to the outside Cainite world.
  • Viziers ("the scholar caste") — academicians, diplomats, and administrators who tend the clan's mortal and Kindred relations.
  • Sorcerers — the clan's blood magicians, the oldest organized practitioners of blood sorcery of any clan, originally raised by Haqim to hunt the demon-worshipping @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali}.

The Eldest: The supreme leader of the clan, seated upon the Black Throne at Alamut, answerable only to Haqim himself. Historically the eldest available fourth-generation childe of Haqim; when none was available, the du'at selected one of their own number. The Eldest can only be deposed by unanimous challenge of all three du'at members — a circumstance recorded only once (Jamal, Eldest 1494–1998, was destroyed by the ancient ur-Shulgi in the event called the Breaking).

The Du'at: The clan's ruling council, composed of the heads of the three castes: the Caliph (leader of the warriors, expected to be the clan's foremost combatant and champion in trial-by-combat; a warrior may ritually challenge a sitting Caliph for the position, with the defeated Caliph submitting to ritual diablerie or facing the rising sun by choice, and the challenger's own childer facing exile or destruction if the challenge fails), the Vizier (elected every 63 years by simple majority of the vizier caste, gathering votes at Alamut on the seventh winter solstice; currently Tegyrius), and the Amr (leader of the sorcerers, traditionally re-selected every year at the vernal equinox by a night-long divination ritual; the position has been held by al-Ashrad continuously since roughly A.D. 120).

The Silsila (also "shakari," the Keepers of the Blood): a small warrior-priesthood of the clan's most devout adherents to Haqim's Laws (and, depending on Alamut's politics, the Path of Blood). They serve as keepers of Alamut's library and museum and as the Mountain's core defenders, and historically acted as the du'at's direct subordinates.

The Council of Scrolls: The joint administrative and academic body of the vizier and sorcerer castes, which approves new blood-sorcery paths and rituals for clan-wide use and reviews new scholarly/scientific developments. It traditionally holds 15 seats, each held by the clan's foremost authority in that field (mathematics, electricity/computing, information-gathering, natural sciences, theology, weapons technology, transportation, chemistry/alchemy, necromancy/spiritualism, economics, archaeology, mortal politics, linguistics, astronomy, and medicine). New rituals must be translated into at least two of the clan's five approved scholarly languages (Latin, Arabic, English, Swahili, and Sanskrit) before being taught clan-wide. The council fractured with the Schism and has not reconvened.

Caste ranks (warriors): drawn from the terminology of the historical mortal Assassin sect — fida'i ("devotee," a newly Embraced or unproven warrior), rafiq ("comrade," a warrior who has proven himself capable and reliable), da'i ("summoner/missionary," a rafiq ordained in a religion, or one who has attained a rating of 7 or more in a Path of Enlightenment and can teach it — in the modern nights almost always a strict Path of Blood adherent), and the informal Westernized ace (a rafiq who has killed five or more non-Assamite vampires of equal or greater power).

Caste ranks (viziers and sorcerers): evaluated jointly by the Council of Scrolls using equivalent benchmarks — aspirant (any unproven member), associate (mortal-equivalent of a doctoral degree in the chosen field), master (full proficiency at the highest levels of the field, demonstrated by an original contribution such as a treatise or new ritual), distinguished master (mastery extended to a second, related field; for sorcerers, full mastery of a second Assamite Sorcery path at Level Five), full master (complete mastery of a primary field plus at least three related fields; for sorcerers, mastery of at least three additional paths and expansive knowledge of rituals), and emeritus (an honorific appended to master or higher, denoting withdrawal from active clan affairs, most often through torpor or declared dispossessed status).

The Darkening: Unlike other Kindred, who pale with age, Assamites darken. After the initial two-to-five-year post-Embrace pallor fades, an Assamite's skin begins to darken between 50 and 100 years after the Embrace, reaching an obsidian-black, faintly glossy hue by roughly the first millennium of unlife; a knowledgeable observer with reference materials can estimate an Assamite's age within about 50 years from skin tone alone. Frequent diablerie measurably accelerates the Darkening, throwing off such estimates. Notably, the Amr al-Ashrad alone among the Children retains pale skin, a fact even he has never explained.

The Tithe: A warrior-caste tradition dating to the era of European mercenary work, wherein a warrior paid for a contract sends a portion of his earnings to his sire, both to enrich the clan as a whole and to honor the sire who trained and judged him into unlife. Apocryphally attributed to the Caliph Mohara's sarcastic rebuke of his childer for taking mercenary work.

Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite}, Chapter Two ("Prayers to Broken Stone"), sidebar "In Nights Past: The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} Curse."

This is the historical clan weakness that applied to every @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} (all three castes) from the ritual enacted under the Treaty of Tyre in 1496 until the event called the Breaking in late 1998, when the ancient ur-Shulgi shattered the curse. Storytellers running chronicles set before the Breaking should use this weakness in place of the modern Path of Blood-era thirst compulsion described elsewhere in this system's Assamite materials.

  • Cainite vitae is a corrosive poison to all Assamites: no Assamite gains any sustenance from drinking the blood of another Kindred.
  • Every point of Cainite blood an Assamite imbibes inflicts one automatic health level of lethal damage.
  • A diablerie attempt inflicts automatic aggravated damage on the would-be diablerist, one health level per point of the victim's permanent Willpower, and the Assamite gains no benefit whatsoever from the act (including no generation reduction) even if he survives it.
  • All three castes' auras remain visibly "stained" during this period exactly as in the modern nights, though this was considered a comparatively minor liability at the time.
  • The sorcerer and vizier castes' other caste-specific weaknesses remain in effect on top of this curse.

Politically, the curse was administered as surety under the Treaty of Tyre (see that page in this compendium) and was treated by @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} elders as proof that Assamites could no longer diablerize Kindred, easing (if never fully resolving) @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} paranoia about the clan. Breaking the curse was the clan's overriding preoccupation for five centuries, occupying successive generations of the Amr and the sorcerer caste's Council of Scrolls seat-holders until ur-Shulgi's sudden unilateral success.
